notes: Equipment + commissioning cost per single charger unit. Site civils, transformer share, and CSMS are computed separately in the setup calculator. Throughput numbers assume an average EV battery at 50% SoC start and 80% SoC stop (ie. 30% of battery capacity delivered per session).

chargers.label: Bharat AC-001
chargers.best_use: Residential, fleet depot overnight, MTC bus depot trickle.
benefits: Lowest CapEx — pays back in <12 months even at modest utilization.
Minimal grid burden — fits on a 1-phase LT connection.
Compatible with the widest installed-base of 2W/3W EVs in TN.
chargers.best_usage_timing: Overnight 10 pm – 6 am; off-peak tariff slot.

chargers.label: Type 2 AC 7.4 kW
vehicles: e-4W passenger (Tata Tiago, Nexon, MG ZS, BYD)
chargers.best_use: Home wallbox, apartment podium parking, mall overnight.
benefits: Universal Type-2 connector standard for all new Indian 4W EVs.
Single-phase install — no HT upgrade needed.
Low maintenance, ~12-year service life.
chargers.best_usage_timing: Overnight + workday office hours (8 am – 6 pm).
limitations: ~5 hr session — not for in-route top-ups.

chargers.label: Type 2 AC 11 kW (3φ)
chargers.best_use: Office parking, tech park, hotel destination charging.
benefits: Roughly halves the AC-7.4 session time.
3-phase balanced load — friendlier on the DT.
chargers.best_usage_timing: Workday 9 am – 6 pm or hotel overnight stay.
limitations: Requires 3-phase LT supply at the site.

chargers.label: Type 2 AC 22 kW (3φ)
chargers.best_use: Mall, restaurant, hotel, F&B destination — couples with 1-3 hr dwell time.
benefits: Best AC option — full top-up in 2 hours.
Cheaper than even the smallest DC chargers.
Long lifecycle, minimal cooling needs.
chargers.best_usage_timing: Peak retail hours 11 am – 10 pm; dynamic pricing recommended.
limitations: Many sub-15-lakh 4Ws have only 7.4 kW onboard — actual throughput limited.

chargers.label: Bharat DC-001 (GB/T 15 kW)
vehicles: e-3W, e-rickshaw, small e-2W swap-station feed
chargers.best_use: Auto-stands, e-rickshaw depots, last-mile delivery hubs.
benefits: Cheapest DC option; pays back fastest in dense 3W belts (Madurai, Trichy, Chennai-North).
Lower-voltage = cheaper power electronics + safer install.
chargers.best_usage_timing: Throughout day — 3W fleet has high duty cycle.
limitations: GB/T connector — limited support on new 4Ws.

chargers.label: CCS2 DC 30 kW
vehicles: e-4W small (Tata Tigor EV, Punch EV, MG Comet)
chargers.best_use: Urban neighborhood, residential complex shared bay, kirana plazas.
benefits: Sweet spot for small DC — under-1-hour top-ups.
Compact footprint, often pole-mountable.
limitations: Underpowered for highway use or large packs.

chargers.label: CCS2 DC 60 kW
vehicles: all current Indian e-4W passenger; e-LCV
benefits: Workhorse of Indian public DC — broad vehicle compatibility.
30-45 min full top-up matches typical mall dwell time.
Make-in-India options available under FAME-II PLI.
chargers.best_usage_timing: Daytime peak 10 am – 9 pm; tariff INR 18-22 / kWh sustainable.
limitations: Highway use only as overflow / lower-power bay.

chargers.label: CCS2 DC 120 kW
vehicles: mid-range e-4W (BYD Atto, Mahindra BE, Hyundai Kona)
chargers.best_use: Urban premium hub, highway entry plaza, fleet rapid-turnaround.
benefits: 20-30 min sessions — passenger-friendly for highway dashes.
Liquid-cooled gun supports continuous duty.
Future-proof for vehicles up to ~150 kW peak.
chargers.best_usage_timing: All-day; peak utilization 11 am – 10 pm on highway, 7-9 pm in city.

chargers.label: CCS2 DC 180 kW
vehicles: premium e-4W (Volvo XC40, BMW iX, BYD Seal)
chargers.best_use: NH48 / NH44 highway plazas, intercity flagship sites.
benefits: Sub-25-min sessions enable 700 km/day intercity travel.
Eligible for higher CapEx subsidy under PM-eDrive highway scheme.
chargers.best_usage_timing: Weekday morning + weekend leisure traffic windows.
limitations: Vehicle pool that can accept 180 kW is still small (<15 %).

chargers.label: CCS2 DC 240 kW Ultra-Fast
vehicles: premium e-4W with 800 V architecture (Kia EV6 GT, Porsche Taycan, Hyundai IONIQ 5/6)
chargers.best_use: Highway flagship — Krishnagiri, Sriperumbudur, Vellore, Salem.
benefits: 15-20 min full top-up — best brand experience.
Pulls high-tariff customers; INR 24-28 / kWh sustainable.
Maximum subsidy stack under PM-eDrive.
chargers.best_usage_timing: All daylight hours on highway; weekend evenings.
limitations: High CapEx; needs 500+ kVA HT connection and on-site BESS recommended.

chargers.label: CCS2 DC 350 kW Hyper-Fast
chargers.best_use: Logistics yards, intercity bus terminals (Koyambedu, Salem, Madurai).
benefits: Required for commercial e-trucks (Eicher Pro 2049, Tata Ace Pro) to be viable on intercity routes.
Pre-positions you for MCS upgrade (1000 kW).
chargers.best_usage_timing: Night cycle for freight fleet (10 pm – 6 am) + scheduled bus windows.
limitations: Demand still emerging — utilization <10% in 2024-25; subsidy-dependent.

chargers.label: CHAdeMO 50 kW
vehicles: older Nissan Leaf, Tata e-Tigor EV (CHAdeMO variant)
benefits: Bi-directional V2G capable (CHAdeMO 2.0).
limitations: CHAdeMO is being deprecated in India; not recommended for new sites.
